newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria recalls officer from Bosnia in racism row.
newsitem.headline: Austria recalls officer from Bosnia in racism row.

text.p: An Austrian army officer was recalled from Bosnia because of racist "wog" T-shirts worn by his peacekeeping troops, the Defence Ministry said on Wednesday.
He had been relieved of his duties for tolerating the offensive t-shirts, it said.

"The ministry has decided to repatriate the platoon commander...The soldiers ordered the T-shirts on their own initiative but the commander was aware of it and did nothing against it," a ministry spokesman said.
The military banned the 30 shirts, inscribed with the name of the peacekeeping Implementation Force, IFOR, and the legend: "Wogs go quiet when our strong arm dictates. Heavy Platoon".
The Austrian pejorative Tschuschen, used in the text, refers particularly to people from the Balkans.
A caricature of far-right Austrian Freedom Party leader Joerg Haider flexing his muscles, a workman's hammer slung across his shoulder, was also emblazoned across the vests.

"The decision to relieve the commander of his duties follows a preliminary report. A final report will be ready in the next two days and further disciplinary proceedings may follow," the ministry spokesman told Reuters.
He declined to name the commander, who headed number three platoon of Austria's transport corps in Bosnia as part of the NATO-led peacekeeping operation there.

Environmentalist Greens politician Edith Zeitz, who spotted two soldiers wearing the shirts in a Croatia-Vienna train at the weekend, told Reuters she expected a full explanation from Defence Minister Werner Fasslabend and she called on Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel to break his silence.

"Fasslabend must tell the Austrian people how this scandal came about and then he must inform the United Nations ...Schuessel must make his position clear because this incident is damaging to Austria's image abroad," she said.
Schuessel and Fasslabend are members of the conservative People's Party, which governs in coalition with Chancellor Franz Vranitzky's Social Democrats.
Fasslabend, describing the T-shirts as "foolish", has argued that only a small number of troops were involved and criticised media for paying too much attention to the incident.
Some Social Democrats said they were far from happy with the official response, however, and one regional politician called on Fasslabend to resign.

Charities working with foreigners and groups representing immigrants from the former Yugoslavia also criticised the defence ministry's handling of the issue and said the T-shirts were a symptom of deep-seated racism in Austria.

"The debate about foreigners and the comments of some politicians create a climate for nationalist and racist ideas," said Peter Quendler of the charity "Neighbour in Need" that aims to help war-torn Bosnia.

Nationalist leader Haider, whose Freedom Party has the backing of a quarter of the electorate, has repeatedly urged an end to immigration and argued that foreigners should be reunited with their families abroad, not in Austria.
